answers.q: How much electricity does one ChatGPT question use?

guess.prompt: One short ChatGPT question uses about as much electricity as…
options: A US home for a day

answers.result: About 2% of a phone charge
answers.reveal: One phone charge, about 19 Wh, is 10 to 80 short questions, depending on whose figure you use.
answers.world: It adds up because there are so many: ChatGPT alone handled 18 billion messages a week by July 2025. At 0.34 Wh each, that’s about 0.32 TWh a year by Hum’s sums. All the world’s data centres together used about 485 TWh in 2025.
answers.share: One ChatGPT question uses about 2% of a phone charge (0.34 Wh, OpenAI’s figure). Billions of them add up: data centres used about 485 TWh in 2025.

answers.q: Does asking ChatGPT use 10 times more energy than a Google search?
answers.heard: “Asking ChatGPT uses 10 times the energy of a Google search.”
answers.result: Out of date
answers.reveal: The 10× compared an early estimate with a figure from 2009. On today’s figures they’re roughly level.
answers.world: All the world’s data centres, of which AI is one part, used about 485 TWh in 2025. That’s about as much electricity as France uses in a year, and around 1.5% of the world’s. The IEA expects it to roughly double by 2030.
answers.share: “ChatGPT uses 10× a Google search” is out of date: newer figures put a short question at roughly 0.3 Wh, level with Google’s 2009 search figure.

answers.q: Does ChatGPT use a bottle of water for every email it writes?
answers.heard: “ChatGPT drinks a bottle of water for every email it writes.”
answers.result: Not for the model that was measured. For today’s, nobody has published it
answers.reveal: The peer-reviewed study said one 500 ml bottle per 10 to 50 answers, for GPT-3.
answers.world: Water is felt locally. In a recent year, US data centres used about 17 billion gallons on site, and about 211 billion more through the power plants that supplied them (Berkeley Lab estimates).
answers.share: “A bottle of water per ChatGPT email”: the study behind it said one 500 ml bottle per 10 to 50 answers, for GPT-3. For today’s models, nobody has published it.

range.claimWhat: what the claim says: a whole bottle

answers.q: Is asking ChatGPT worse than streaming Netflix?
answers.heard: “One ChatGPT question uses more energy than an hour of Netflix.”
answers.heardFrom: a common worry in comment threads
answers.result: No: an hour of streaming is about 41 to 230 questions
answers.reveal: An hour of Netflix, about 77 Wh in 2019 by the IEA’s estimate, is about 230 short questions at OpenAI’s figure.
answers.world: All the world’s data centres, of which AI is one part, used about 485 TWh in 2025. That’s about as much electricity as France uses in a year, and around 1.5% of the world’s. The IEA expects it to roughly double by 2030.
answers.share: An hour of Netflix used about as much electricity as 41 to 230 short ChatGPT questions (IEA, 2019; OpenAI and MIT Technology Review figures).

answers.q: Is using AI worse for the climate than taking a flight?
answers.heard: “Using AI is as bad for the climate as flying.”
answers.result: No, for ordinary chatting
answers.reveal: One 1,000 km domestic flight is roughly a million short questions.
answers.world: All the world’s data centres, of which AI is one part, used about 485 TWh in 2025. That’s about as much electricity as France uses in a year, and around 1.5% of the world’s. The IEA expects it to roughly double by 2030.
answers.share: One 1,000 km domestic flight is about 0.8 to 1.5 million short AI questions in CO₂ (UK factors via Our World in Data; OpenAI’s 0.34 Wh; world-average grid).

answers.q: Do “thinking” modes use more energy than normal answers?
answers.heard: “Thinking modes use far more energy than a normal answer.”
answers.result: Yes, often far more
answers.reveal: Measured on open models: about 30 times more on average.
answers.world: One person’s share is small, but the total keeps growing: electricity use by AI-focused data centres grew 50% in 2025, by the IEA’s estimate.
answers.share: Thinking modes use far more energy: about 30× more on average in Hugging Face’s measurements of open models, and 150 to 700× for the same model with reasoning on.

answers.q: How much does my ChatGPT use add to my carbon footprint in a year?

guess.prompt: A typical ChatGPT user’s year of questions makes about…

answers.result: About 0.2 kg of CO₂ a year
answers.reveal: About 26 questions a week at 0.34 Wh each, on the world-average grid.
answers.world: One person’s share is small, but the total keeps growing: electricity use by AI-focused data centres grew 50% in 2025, by the IEA’s estimate.
answers.share: A typical ChatGPT user’s year of questions: about 0.2 kg of CO₂ (Hum’s sums from OpenAI’s figures). The build-out behind it is growing fast: AI data centres used 50% more electricity in 2025.

answers.q: Are big tech companies’ emissions going up because of AI?
answers.heard: “Big tech’s emissions are rising because of AI.”
answers.heardFrom: news coverage of the companies’ reports
answers.result: Rising, yes. How much is AI, they don’t say
answers.reveal: Google’s emissions rose 18% in 2025, and Microsoft’s 25% in its 2025 fiscal year, by their own reports.
answers.world: All the world’s data centres, of which AI is one part, used about 485 TWh in 2025. That’s about as much electricity as France uses in a year, and around 1.5% of the world’s. The IEA expects it to roughly double by 2030.
answers.share: By their own reports: Google’s emissions rose 18% in 2025 (electricity use up 37%), Microsoft’s 25% in fiscal 2025. How much is AI, they don’t say.

answers.q: Are data centres making my electricity bill go up?
answers.heard: “Data centres are pushing up everyone’s electricity bills.”
answers.result: Partly: in the eastern US, the grid’s monitor says yes
answers.reveal: In the PJM grid of the eastern US, the independent market monitor calls data-centre load growth the primary reason capacity prices jumped.
answers.world: Across US states from 2019 to 2025, Berkeley Lab found those with the highest demand growth generally saw average prices fall after inflation, and says data-centre load doesn’t appear to change that. In PJM, the market monitor’s estimates point to data centres pushing capacity costs up.
answers.share: PJM’s independent market monitor estimates data-centre load raised the eastern US grid’s 2026/2027 capacity auction revenue by $7.3 billion (82.1%). What reaches your bill depends on your utility and state.

answers.q: Are data centres powered by coal, gas or renewables?

guess.prompt: Which source supplies the most electricity to the world’s data centres today?

answers.result: Mostly fossil fuels: coal about 30%, gas 26%
answers.reveal: Coal is the largest single source at about 30%, then renewables at 27%, gas at 26% and nuclear at 15%.
answers.world: Looking ahead, the IEA expects renewables to meet about half of the growth in data-centre demand.
answers.share: The world’s data centres run mostly on fossil fuels: about 30% coal and 26% gas, with 27% renewables and 15% nuclear (IEA, Energy and AI 2025).

answers.q: What share of the world’s electricity do data centres use?

guess.prompt: What share of the world’s electricity did data centres use in 2024?

answers.result: About 1.5%
answers.reveal: About 415 TWh in 2024, and 485 TWh in 2025: about as much as France uses in a year.
answers.world: The IEA expects data centres to use about 950 TWh by 2030, roughly double 2025.
answers.share: Data centres used about 1.5% of the world’s electricity in 2024 (IEA). By 2025 that was about as much as France uses in a year, and the IEA expects it to roughly double by 2030.

answers.q: Will AI cut more emissions than it causes?
answers.heard: “AI will cut more emissions than it causes.”
answers.heardFrom: a common argument for building more AI
answers.result: It could, in a forecast. Nobody has measured it
answers.reveal: In the IEA’s wide-adoption scenario, AI tools cut around 5% of energy-related emissions in 2035. That depends on uptake the IEA says has no momentum yet.
answers.world: Data centres’ own emissions, from the electricity they consume, were about 180 million tonnes of CO₂ in the IEA’s 2025 report, heading for 300 Mt by 2035 in its Base Case and up to 500 Mt in its Lift-Off Case. That stays below 1.5% of energy-sector emissions.
answers.share: Will AI cut more emissions than it causes? In an IEA scenario, yes: around 5% of energy-related emissions in 2035 if AI tools are widely used. But that’s a forecast, and the IEA calls AI “not a silver bullet”.

answers.q: Why do people near data centres hear a constant hum, and how loud can it be?

guess.prompt: In Fairfax County, Virginia, the night-time limit for steady noise in residential areas, which a new data centre must show it meets, is…

answers.result: Up to 55 dBA at night, in one Virginia county
answers.reveal: A noise expert says people call 55 to 65 decibels no louder than conversation. The trouble, residents say, is that it never stops.
answers.world: Near a cluster of Amazon data centres in Prince William County, Virginia, measurements found the noise below the county’s 60-decibel daytime limit about half the time. Residents still said the constant drone, especially at night, cost them sleep. Amazon was muffling its cooling equipment, the local paper reported.
answers.share: Why data centres hum: their cooling runs night and day. Fairfax County, Virginia, caps steady noise in residential areas at 55 dBA at night; Chandler, Arizona, says new ones can’t be louder than the background.

answers.q: Do data centres use drinking water?
answers.result: Mostly, at Google: about 78% of its data-centre water was drinking-quality
answers.reveal: Google’s data centres took in about 37 billion litres of water in 2024, and about 29 billion of it was potable, by Google’s own report.
answers.world: Across the US, data centres consumed about 17 billion gallons of water on site in a recent year (a Berkeley Lab estimate). Nobody publishes how much of that was drinking water.
answers.share: Google’s data centres drew about 29 billion litres of potable, drinking-quality water in 2024, about 78% of their total, by Google’s own report. Some sites run on reclaimed wastewater.

answers.q: Will more efficient AI chips fix AI’s energy problem?
answers.heard: “More efficient AI chips will fix AI’s energy problem.”
answers.result: Not on their own
answers.reveal: Each AI answer uses far less energy than it did, but use is growing faster, so the total keeps rising.
answers.world: The world’s data centres used about 485 TWh in 2025, about as much electricity as France uses in a year. The IEA expects that to roughly double to 950 TWh by 2030.
answers.share: More efficient chips won’t fix AI’s energy use on their own: energy per AI task is falling fast, yet data-centre electricity grew 17% in 2025, and even the IEA’s High Efficiency case reaches about 970 TWh by 2035.

answers.q: Are tech companies restarting Three Mile Island to power AI?
answers.heard: “Tech companies are restarting Three Mile Island to power AI.”
answers.heardFrom: news coverage since the 2024 Microsoft deal
answers.result: Unit 1, for Microsoft’s data centres, and not running yet
answers.reveal: It’s Unit 1, not Unit 2, the reactor in the 1979 accident. Constellation expects it online in 2027.
answers.world: Once running, it would restore 835 megawatts to the grid, Constellation says. All the world’s data centres, of which AI is one part, used about 485 TWh of electricity in 2025.
answers.share: Three Mile Island: Unit 1 (not the 1979 accident reactor) is being restarted under a 20-year deal for Microsoft’s data centres. It isn’t running yet; Constellation expects 2027.

answers.q: How much electricity does making an AI picture or video use?

guess.prompt: One short AI video clip uses about as much electricity as…
options: A US home for a day

answers.result: About 90 Wh: like boiling a litre of water
answers.reveal: In one lab test, a short clip from an open video model used about 90 Wh (Hugging Face). Boiling a litre of water takes about 99 Wh.
answers.world: Nobody publishes how many AI pictures and videos are made, or what they use in total. All the world’s data centres, of which AI is one part, used about 485 TWh in 2025, and the IEA expects about 950 TWh by 2030.
answers.share: One short AI video clip used about 90 Wh in a lab test on an open model (Hugging Face), about as much as boiling a litre of water. One AI picture: about 0.63 to 1.22 Wh (MIT Technology Review).

answers.q: Does saying “please” and “thank you” to ChatGPT waste energy?
answers.heard: “Saying please and thank you to ChatGPT costs tens of millions of dollars in electricity.”
answers.heardFrom: a viral reply by OpenAI’s CEO on X, April 2025
answers.result: A little. The “tens of millions” was a quip
answers.reveal: Altman’s “tens of millions of dollars” came with no calculation. A stand-alone thank-you costs about as much as any short message: 0.34 Wh or less, by OpenAI’s average.
answers.world: ChatGPT handled 18 billion messages a week by July 2025: about 0.32 TWh a year at 0.34 Wh each, by Hum’s sums. All the world’s data centres used about 485 TWh in 2025.
answers.share: Saying “thank you” to ChatGPT costs about as much as any short message: 0.34 Wh or less, by OpenAI’s figure. Sam Altman’s “tens of millions of dollars” was a quip, not a calculation.

answers.q: Does big tech really run on 100% renewable energy?
answers.result: On paper over a year, yes. Hour by hour, no
answers.reveal: Google matched 100% of its 2025 electricity use with renewable purchases over the year, but hour by hour its data centres and offices ran on about 65% carbon-free energy, by its own figures.
answers.world: Worldwide, the grids data centres draw from supply about 30% of their electricity from coal and 26% from gas, with about 27% from renewables, by the IEA’s estimate. A peer-reviewed Princeton study of the western US grid found that matching a year’s use has minimal impact on long-run emissions, while matching it hour by hour can cut them significantly.
answers.share: “100% renewable” is a yearly sum on paper. Google matched 100% of its 2025 electricity that way, but hour by hour on local grids it ran on about 65% carbon-free energy, by its own figures.

answers.q: Should I stop using ChatGPT to help the planet?
answers.heard: “Using ChatGPT is bad for the planet.”
answers.heardFrom: said at school, at parties and online
answers.result: Small for you, big in total
answers.reveal: A typical user’s year of questions makes about 0.2 kg of CO₂, roughly half a mile in a US car. The total is what’s large: data centres used about 485 TWh in 2025.
answers.world: All the world’s data centres consumed about 485 TWh of electricity in 2025, and the IEA expects about 950 TWh by 2030. Electricity use by AI-focused data centres grew 50% in 2025. How much CO₂ that makes depends on where the power comes from: the IEA expects renewables to meet half of the growth.
answers.share: Is using ChatGPT bad for the planet? Partly: a typical user’s year of questions makes about 0.2 kg of CO₂, roughly half a mile in a US car (Hum’s sums). The total is the big part: data centres used about 485 TWh in 2025 (IEA).

answers.q: Which uses more electricity: training AI, or people using it?

guess.prompt: Where a company has published the split, which took more of its machine-learning energy?

answers.result: Using it, where anyone has measured
answers.reveal: At Google, about three fifths of machine-learning energy went on use and two fifths on training, in the three years before 2022.
answers.world: Use adds up fast: ChatGPT alone got about 2.6 billion messages a day by July 2025, by Hum’s sums from OpenAI’s count. All the world’s data centres together used about 485 TWh in 2025.
answers.share: Where it’s been measured, using AI takes more energy than training it: about three fifths of Google’s machine-learning energy went on use (Google, 2022).
